Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Leah (NimbusFlow Lead Eng), Omar (CTO), Sanita (Product), Jin (SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be fuzzy): Quick sync to review the POC's function-calling flows, SDK integration sanity checks, structured-output contract mismatches seen in staging, and next steps for benchmarking latency and fallback behavior. Some small transcription errors likely.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. can you all hear me okay?
[00:03] Omar: yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Leah: good. first time we've had the full team in one sync.
[00:12] Maya: awesome. agenda: quick status, show a tiny SDK snippet for invoke patterns, discuss observed mismatches in structured output, then agree next steps. carlos will cover latency knobs.
[00:30] Carlos: hi team. quick note: we looked at your staging traces, saw that most of the calls use tool-invoke for search then fallback to open model for summarization, which is expected. found a couple of cases where the function signature didn't match the contract - looked like the schema had an extra field 'user_intent' spelled 'user intent' in one call.
[01:05] Leah: yeah that was from our side, we changed the frontend adapter last week. some of the structured outputs are being stringified which makes the downstream parser choke.
[01:22] Sanita: product question - are we intended to always call the tool first then the model? or sometimes call model directly?
[01:30] Maya: good question. the recommended pattern for your use case is tool-first for retrieval-heavy flows (search, db-lookup), then a model invoke for synthesis. but the SDK supports direct model calls when you want inline generation. you can toggle by route.
[01:50] Jin: our SRE saw a spike in outbound connections when the tool callback retries happened, looked like retries were set to 5 in the adapter. that's creating bursty egress.
[02:10] Carlos: yep, that's a config thing. our SDK defaults to 2 retries for callbacks; looks like the customer's adapter reconfigured it. we can show a guarded retry helper in the snippet.
[02:28] Leah: can you show the snippet now?
[02:32] Maya: sure, i'll share my screen — pasted into chat: https://redwood.ai/shared/sdk/structured-output-example (note: link is illustrative).
[02:40] Maya: snippet (verbatim-ish):

const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const res = await client.invoke({
  model: 'rwd-3b',
  input: prompt,
  tools: [ 'search', 'inventory_lookup' ],
  structured_output: { schema: 'order_summary_v1' },
  on_tool_call: (tool, params) => { ... },
  fallback: { model: 'rwd-1b-quant', rules: [ 'latency>300 -> fallback' ] }
});

[03:25] Carlos: couple of things to highlight: the structured_output block attaches a contract and the runtime validates return shapes, but the SDK won't auto-cast strings into objects if your tool returns JSON-as-string. you need to use tools that return application/json content-type or run a post-processor.
[03:50] Leah: that's exactly what we're seeing. our legacy tool returns a text payload.
[03:55] Maya: two immediate options: update tool to send proper content-type, or use the SDK's 'parseJsonField' helper we can include in the sample. i'll add that to the snippet.
[04:12] Omar: is there an automatic fallback if validation fails? we'd prefer not to fail the whole request.
[04:18] Carlos: yes, you can set structured_output.on_violation to 'coerce' or 'warn_and_continue' or 'error'. default is 'error' in strict mode. for POC i'd suggest 'warn_and_continue' then log the mismatch to your telemetry.
[04:40] Sanita: product follow up — what are typical latencies when using tool-first with a search+model? our SLO is 300ms p95 for quick replies.
[04:52] Carlos: in our hosted runs with batching off for low latency, search + model is often 180-350ms depending on tool backend. if your search backend is slow (100-200ms) that pushes it. we can show batching knobs but note batching trades off latency for throughput.
[05:20] Jin: about caching — can Redwood's KV cache be used to cache intermediate tool results?
[05:25] Maya: yes, prefix caching works. you can key by query hash to avoid repeated search calls. that cut our test costs and latency in similar POCs. we'll include a small recommend config.
[05:40] Leah: on structured output mismatches, we had one case where the model returned a list instead of an object, which caused our parser to throw. it happened when the model hallucinated an alternate schema.
[05:58] Carlos: that suggests the model prompt needs stronger guardrails. two practical fixes: 1) pin the model to a version with better JSON compliance, 2) add a pre- and post-validation step — SDK example will show both.
[06:20] Omar: can the runtime auto-rewrite to coerce types? for example if a field expected number but got string, can it coerce?
[06:28] Carlos: yes, coerce rules exist but they're conservative. we avoid silent coercion for critical fields. you can configure per-field rules in the contract.
[06:45] Maya: quick demo of tool callbacks — the SDK uses a callback URL pattern. tool calls are executed server-side, and the return gets stitched into the model context. if your tools are behind VPC, you can use our callback proxy or an SQS-based puller.
[07:05] Jin: for us the SQS puller is preferred. any extra steps?
[07:09] Carlos: just ensure the IAM role has permissions and the callback secret is rotated. we'll share the minimal infra checklist.
[07:20] Leah: the other oddity we saw was streaming responses sometimes cut the final closing brace for JSON. maybe because the client consumed partial stream.
[07:32] Maya: streaming partials are tricky. SDK has a 'stream-accumulate-then-validate' helper that buffers until end-of-stream, but that increases latency. alternative is chunk-aware parser that can validate partial JSON, but both options have tradeoffs.
[07:55] Sanita: product perspective — if we pick the buffer approach, how do we keep the UX snappy?
[08:00] Carlos: you can stream a minimal placeholder response to the UI and then patch with the structured data when validated. UX team can show a spinner.
[08:12] Omar: let's talk about fallback model selection; we saw more expensive model being hit during peak which increased costs.
[08:18] Maya: our smart routing can prefer cheaper model families for non-critical routes. in SDK you can set route-level policies like {cost_budget: 0.002, prefer: ['rwd-1b-quant'] } so at runtime it will pick compatible variant.
[08:36] Leah: will that impact quality for tasks like summarization?
[08:40] Carlos: yes slightly. best practice: tag routes by SLA and quality. critical routes pinned to higher-quality models. background or non-user-facing routes use cheaper variants.
[08:55] Jin: about telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdown per request to attribute to product area. can we get that?
[09:02] Maya: yes, Console exposes token-level cost and per-route aggregation. we can also stream tracehooks to your datadog. we'll include a sample trace mapping.
[09:18] Leah: thanks. on the mismatched schema earlier, Carlos you mentioned pre-validation — can you walk through the sample flow?
[09:24] Carlos: sure. flow: tool call -> SDK parses tool result -> run lightweight schema validation (fast) -> if passes attach to prompt else run sanitizer (coerce, trim fields) -> model call with sanitized context. we'll add a code snippet for that.
[09:55] Omar: any security concerns with sanitizer running arbitrary code?
[10:00] Carlos: sanitizer runs in-user process, not in Redwood tenant; for Private deployments you control it. for hosted, we provide a vetted sanitizer lib. but for sensitive data, best to keep it inside your VPC and use Private deployment.
[10:20] Sanita: timeline question — if we decide on Private deployment later, how hard is it to move?
[10:26] Maya: we have migration patterns. many customers start in hosted with strict TOS and then move to Dedicated or Private once they commit. we can map the steps and what changes (networking, KMS).
[10:40] Leah: operationally, we hit a bug where the SDK retried model calls on 5xx and doubled the token usage — that spiked our bill.
[10:52] Carlos: interesting. default retry logic is conservative, but if your adapter obscured 429/500 semantics, it can cause more retries. we'll show safe retry wrappers. add a header x-rw-id to dedupe retries.
[11:12] Maya: next please — sample of structured-output contract mismatch that happened: posted in the CRM a snippet. gist showed model returning 'items' as string instead of array.
[11:25] Leah: yes that's the one.
[11:30] Carlos: actionable: add a preflight validation in the SDK that normalizes types and logs telemetry. also run model scoring on a curated prompt set to catch regressions.
[11:45] Omar: will Redwood run a quick eval on our prompt set?
[11:50] Maya: yes, we can run an eval in ~24-48 hours if you share prompts and expected outputs. that'll show baseline pass rate and highlight where models hallucinate structure.
[12:03] Sanita: customer asks: what's the recommended default for structured_output.on_violation for production?
[12:09] Carlos: 'warn_and_continue' for non-critical, 'error' for strict flows. and enforce post-checks in clients.
[12:22] Leah: anything we should change in our staging harness to make tests more deterministic?
[12:27] Carlos: pin seed values, pin model versions, and reduce randomness by setting temperature=0 for contract checks. also run many short runs to catch flaky cases.
[12:42] Jin: networking note — when using callback proxy there's a 2s added latency; for many small tool calls that accumulates. consider batching tool calls when possible.
[12:55] Maya: quick recap of what we'll send after this call: SDK example with parseJsonField and retry guard, short runbook for VPC/callbacks, and proposed benchmark plan.
[13:10] Omar: sounds good. can we get pricing impact if we add extra validation steps that increase token usage?
[13:18] Maya: yes we'll provide sample cost numbers for the benchmark plan — estimate additional tokens and cost uplift.
[13:30] Leah: final question — are there any known model variants that handle JSON output best?
[13:36] Carlos: rwd-3b v2 in our catalog has improved JSON adherence; also rwd-json-1 tuned for schema outputs. we'll include recommended pins.
[13:50] Sanita: thanks, that's helpful.
[13:55] Maya: ok let's confirm dates — maya will send SDK sample by 2026-02-01, carlos to prepare bench plan by 2026-02-04, leah to run staging tests by 2026-02-05, jin to validate network by 2026-02-03.
[14:10] Omar: agreed. thanks team.
[14:14] Maya: any other q's? otherwise we'll wrap.
[14:18] Leah: none. thanks.
[14:20] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in CRM and share links. bye.
